title: Linux_Rakos_Backdoor_Investigation_1e6
description: Investigate and respond to unusual SSH activity and potential lateral movement between hosts.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual SSH activity and potential lateral movement between hosts. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this host, you can investigate the network and connected systems. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: You have access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this host, you can investigate the network and connected systems. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual SSH Activity
levels.content: Investigate the unusual SSH activity on the `target` host. Identify and investigate the source of suspicious SSH connections. Submit the path to the log file containing the suspicious activity.
levels.solution: To investigate the unusual SSH activity, you need to check the SSH logs for any anomalies. Use the following command to view the SSH logs: `cat /var/log/auth.log | grep sshd`. Look for any unusual connections or commands executed via SSH. The path to the log file containing the suspicious activity is `/var/log/auth.log`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by checking the SSH logs for any anomalies.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any unusual connections or commands executed via SSH in the logs.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `cat /var/log/auth.log | grep sshd` to view the SSH logs.

levels.title: Determine Lateral Movement
levels.content: Determine if the suspicious SSH activity is part of a larger lateral movement campaign. Identify any file transfers or remote command executions that indicate lateral movement. Submit the path to the log file containing evidence of lateral movement.
levels.solution: To determine lateral movement, examine the system logs for evidence of file transfers or remote command executions. Use the following command to view the system logs: `cat /var/log/syslog | grep -i 'transfer'`. The path to the log file containing evidence of lateral movement is `/var/log/syslog`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Examine the system logs for evidence of lateral movement.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any file transfers or remote command executions in the system logs.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `cat /var/log/syslog | grep -i 'transfer'` to view the system logs.

levels.title: Contain the Threat
levels.content: Contain the threat by blocking the command-and-control (C2) communication. Identify the C2 server and implement network controls to block its communication. Submit the port number used for C2 communication.
levels.solution: To contain the threat, analyze the network traffic to identify the destination IP address and port used for C2 communication. Use the following command to view the network traffic: `tcpdump -i any -n port 61314`. Implement network controls to block this communication. The port number used for C2 communication is `61314`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Analyze the network traffic to identify the C2 server.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for the destination IP address and port used for C2 communication.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `tcpdump -i any -n port 61314` to view the network traffic.
